To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new failure mode in gold wire bonds, the high strength ball lift, is observed in gold wire bonds that are aged in air.

the high strength ball lift failure mode is due to degradation of the Au-Au 4 Al interface during ageing in an oxygen containing atmosphere at 175°C, which causes the Au 4 AI compound to grow in an annulus shape that propagates a crack into the Au ball during pull testing.

1) A new failure mode has been identified, termed a high strength (HS) ball lift (BL), 2) The failure mode is due to a partial de-bond between Au ball and intermetallica (Au4Al) and 3) The number of HS BLs and point in time at failure depend on the bonded gold ball height (squash height) and the growth of the de-bond region is believed to be due to a combination of intermetallica degradation
In summary, our research is concerned with
the unusual mechanical failure mode of high strength ball lift and the effect of ball squash height on the occurrence of the failure mode.

the identification and characterisation of a previously unknown failure mode in gold interconnects that is observed to depend critically on bonded ball squash height and which may have implications for reliability testing of gold ballbonds in microelectronics.
a failure mode that is unique to gold ballbonds and which has the potential to impact the reliability of gold ballbonds in high temperature applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Au 4 A1 intermetallic compound has a finite lifetime at 175 °c in air.
the HSBL failure mechanism can be avoided by controlling the ball squash height during bonding.

the HSBL is a unique failure mode that occurs due to a combination of thermo-chemical degradation at the Au 4 A1 interface and the stress field in the Au ball that is generated by a mismatch between the intrinsic growth stresses of the Au ball and Au 4 Al.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HSBL failures are due to a combination of stress-induced and thermo-chemical mechanisms and the HSBL’s can be avoided by careful control of the bonded ball squash heights.

the HSBL failure mode is due to thermochemical degradation of the intermetallical compound and the dependence of failure mode transition on ball squash height is due to a competition between the thermochemical degradation of Au 4 Al, the stress state in the Au ball and the intrinsic growth stresses in the intermetallic.

the failure mode of gold ballbonded devices is dependent on both the bonded ball squash and the bake time and temperature, and can be used to predict the onset of failure for devices with different squash heights.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HSBL failure mode can be avoided by careful control of the bonded ball squash heights and that the HSBL is a unique failure mode that is only encountered in gold ball bonds at 175 ° C.
the HSBL failure mode is an important reliability concern in gold ballbonded packages that are subjected to long-term high temperature exposure in air.
